picks.title: Why did Apple buy AI music startup Samplab, and how might this impact Logic Pro?
picks.rationale: Apple quietly bought AI audio startup Samplab (disclosed in an EU DMA filing), a strong signal that polyphonic audio-to-MIDI and note editing are coming to Logic Pro. Directly actionable for Logic users. Kept over the MusicRadar version of the same story (cluster c0).
picks.excerpt: Apple acquired AI audio startup Samplab (disclosed via an EU Digital Markets Act filing), seemingly to bolster Logic Pro's AI tools such as polyphonic audio-to-MIDI and note editing.

picks.title: IAMDDB accuses Israel of 'stealing her identity' in AI propaganda video
picks.rationale: A new case of an artist's AI-generated likeness being used without consent in a government video. A concrete deepfake and likeness-rights incident that hasn't been covered before.
picks.excerpt: Manchester artist IAMDDB says a now-deleted government clip used an AI-generated likeness of her, raising artist-likeness and deepfake concerns.

picks.title: Romain Gavras Is Bummed About Those AI Versions of 'Storm'
picks.rationale: Director Romain Gavras reacts to AI copycat recreations of his Yung Lean 'Storm' music video. A fresh example of AI imitating music-video craft, and a creator-side view of what it costs the crew behind the original.
picks.excerpt: Director Romain Gavras says AI copycat 'recreations' of his Yung Lean 'Storm' video made him sad for the crew who put in so much work on the real thing.

picks.title: Streaming Fraud Threatens More Than Fraudsters. We Must Find Meaningful Solutions (Guest Column)
picks.rationale: NMPA chief David Israelite argues that AI-fuelled streaming fraud (Deezer counts 90,000 AI tracks a day) is draining songwriter royalties. It is the publishers' formal stance, not a rehash of the earlier Copyright Office inquiry story.
picks.excerpt: NMPA chief David Israelite argues streaming fraud, exacerbated by AI-generated tracks (Deezer: 90,000 a day), drains songwriter royalties and needs industry solutions.

picks.title: Moises and SoundCloud Partner to Bring AI-Supported Creation, Collaboration and Distribution Together for 150+ Million Artists
picks.rationale: A concrete new product partnership: Moises's stem separation, chord and lyric detection, and AI mix/master tools plug into SoundCloud's distribution, with a no-training-without-consent pledge. Directly actionable for independent creators, and a different outlet and angle (tools) from the other four picks.
picks.excerpt: Moises, the ethically trained AI creative suite used by 80 million musicians, is partnering with SoundCloud to bring stem separation, chord/lyric detection and AI-assisted mixing and mastering together with SoundCloud distribution. SoundCloud says it does not train generative models on artists' music without consent.
